$comment: The one place that decides how an intent looks on each platform. The OS is fixed per bundle; the window class (compact, medium, expanded, dual) is live, reported by the host, and re-resolves when the window changes (rotation, unfolding, split screen, Stage Manager). Rendering reaches the host as node types and tones. `weft design explain` reads this file.

idioms.system: Use each platform's own control and placement wherever one exists.
idioms.blend: Default. Chrome and controls follow the platform; content stays warp.
idioms.brand: warp everywhere, identical on web, iOS and Android.

Choice.intent: Pick one of 2–5 short options shown together.

why.warp: warp segmented buttons: the web has no system control for this, and brand asks for warp.
why.segmented: iOS uses a segmented control (UISegmentedControl) for mutually exclusive options within one view.
why.chips: Android has no segmented control in the framework; Material 3 uses choice chips for this.

AppTabs.intent: Switch between the app's top-level sections.

why.header: Section tabs in the header next to the title: the web convention, and the warp layout under brand.
why.tab-bar: iOS puts top-level sections in a tab bar at the bottom, on every iPhone in both orientations and on narrow iPad windows.
why.navigation-bar: Android puts top-level sections in a Material 3 navigation bar at the bottom of compact windows, selected item on a pill indicator.
why.sidebar: A wide iPad window shows top-level sections in a sidebar on the leading edge.
why.navigation-rail: From 600dp Material 3 moves the sections to a navigation rail on the leading edge, so they don't stretch across a wide bottom bar.
why.spanned: Across a separating hinge (on the web, the Viewport Segments API) the first two sections sit side by side, one per pane, and the tab control goes away. This holds under every idiom: a hinge is hardware, not style, so nothing is ever laid out under it.

classes.compact: Width under 600 (pt or dp): every phone in portrait, small split-screen windows.
classes.medium: 600 to 839: phones in landscape, iPad mini in portrait, unfolded foldables, half an iPad.
classes.expanded: 840 and up: tablets and iPads in landscape, desktop windows.
classes.dual: The window spans two panes split by a hinge or fold that separates them (Surface Duo, a foldable in book posture). Wins over width.
